structure.en: it's on my mind, you know?

patterns.name: 〜のだ
patterns.explanation: の at the end of a sentence gives it an explaining, sharing-my-feelings tone; with よ and ね after it, it sounds soft and feminine. きに　なるのよね = 'it's on my mind, you know?'

patterns.name: 〜になる
patterns.explanation: に with なる says what something ends up as. Here it is part of a set phrase about something ending up on your mind. きに　なる = 'it bothers me'.
